channel.title: Block Club Chicago - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Block Club Chicago (blockclubchicago.org)

item.title: Architecture And Design Film Festival Returns To Chicago This Weekend
item.description: Starting Thursday, architecture enthusiasts can watch 10 films about built spaces and the people behind them at the Chicago Cultural Center and the Gene Siskel Film Center.

item.title: Jesse Jackson: A Civil Rights Icon — And To South Shore Residents, Their Neighbor ‘Rev’
item.description: Jackson Park Highlands neighbors remembered the reverend as equal parts political powerhouse and jovial neighbor. They plan to honor him around South Shore with banners, media and reflections on his legacy.

item.title: Fake Spring’s Last Gasp Coming Thursday, With Temps Dropping Into 20s This Weekend
item.description: Wednesday will be a great day to crack windows and go for a stroll — before winter starts creeping back into the picture Friday.

item.title: Outbound Brown Line Trains Will Bypass Western Stop Thursday Through March 1
item.description: Kimball-bound trains will skip the Western stop in Lincoln Square 3 a.m. Thursday-4 a.m. March 1 due to construction, according to Ald. Matt Martin’s office and CTA officials.

item.title: ‘All Are Welcome’ At Rev. Jesse Jackson Memorial, But Family Says To Leave Politics At Home
item.description: Services for the civil rights icon are set to begin next week and will be open to the public, though details are still being finalized.

item.title: Foundry Park Development At Former Lincoln Yards Site Approved By City Council
item.description: Though it's scaled back from the Lincoln Yards megadevelopment project, Foundry Park will bring thousands of new housing units plus retail, office and park space to the former industrial site along the Chicago River.

item.title: 25-Story Residential Tower Proposed For City-Owned Site Near Harold Washington Library
item.description: The city selected DL3 Realty’s $162 million plan to bring 300 mixed-income units, retail and restaurant space to the Plymouth Court site and make improvements to nearby Pritzker Park.

item.title: Amazon Outlines Plans To Turn Central Steel Plant Into Distribution Hub, Not All Neighbors Happy
item.description: Amazon is going forward with plans to demolish the former Central Steel & Wire Plant, 3000 W. 51st St., and replace it with a 230,000-square-foot warehouse.

item.title: Columbus Statue In Little Italy Park To Be Replaced By One Of Mother Cabrini, Park District Says
item.description: Frances Xavier Cabrini, the first American saint, easily won a public vote to determine a replacement statue for the Columbus bust that was controversially removed by the city in 2020.

item.title: City Council Fails To Override Mayor’s Hemp Ban Veto, Rejects Lane-Blocking Ticketing Program
item.description: Wednesday's meeting also saw alderpeople delay an effort to have a police watchdog agency investigate possible violations of the Chicago's Welcoming City ordinance.
